english.title: Drive an unlicensed hackney carriage which plied for hire within the Metropolitan Police District or City of London

english.legislation: Contrary to section 7 of the Metropolitan Public Carriage Act 1869.

english.notes:
(i) The displaying of a sign on a vehicle is not soliciting.
(ii) Courts will take the view that a vehicle plying for hire on private land adjoining a street (e.g. as in an adjacent railway forecourt ) with the purpose of attracting customers from that street, is plying for hire in the street (Eastbourne Borough Council v Stirling and Morley 2000).
(iii) In Oddy v Bugbugs Ltd (2003), a private prosecution on behalf of a Licenced Taxi Drivers Association failed against a company using rickshaws. They do not fall within the meaning of Hackney Carriage.
(iv) It is a defence for the driver to prove that he was ignorant of the fact of the carriage being an unlicensed carriage - the same defence is not available for the owner of the carriage (see H)
